To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neurons in cat V1 respond to feature discontinuities, that the feature type (e.g. phase, orientation) is not critical for the response to a feature border, and that the response can be explained by a model that is based on the interaction of center and surround mechanisms.

neurons in area 17 of the cat are sensitive to borders in their preferred orientation that are created by a difference in phase, orientation, or direction of motion, that the firing of these neurons is increased when such borders are placed near their receptive field, that this increase in firing is partly independent of the type of border involved, and that this increase in response is due to a release from suppression.

neurons in area 17 are sensitive to borders in orientation and phase, but not in direction of motion, that the sensitivity of the neurons to these borders is orientation specific, and that the sensitivity is due to a release from suppression rather than facilitatory interactions.

neurons in V1 can respond to feature boundaries, but that this response is weak compared to the response to a luminance border.
